chunks: And from him, raising it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he taught his brother Abdullah ibn Ali this supplication.

O Allah, raise my expectation upwards, and do not make me an object of covetousness for an enemy or an envier, and protect me while standing and sitting, awake and sleeping. O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, and guide me to Your most straight path, and save me from the heat of Hell, and shake off from me the debt and the sin, and make me from the best of the choicest of the world.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication taught by Imam al-Baqir for protection from enemies and relief from debt?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication highlights the familial transmission of spiritual wisdom from Imam al-Baqir to his brother Abdullah ibn Ali, emphasizing a holistic approach to divine protection. It uniquely combines psychological well-being, such as elevated hope (ظنّي), with practical concerns like debt relief (المغرم), reflecting the Shia tradition of integrating worldly needs with otherworldly salvation. The invocation serves as a comprehensive remedy for both internal spiritual states and external worldly trials.
